## 85d01dd02c6d

**Issue found: ordinary draws omit the internal-wall branch, leaving a canonical shortcut unfalsified.**

`generate` paints color 9 only on the outer border. Across inspected default draws there were zero interior 9 cells, even though four of the five canonical train/test inputs contain interior 9 barriers. Consequently, the wrong rule “a seed sees every cell in its row or column; ignore intervening 9 walls” is exactly equivalent to the authority on every ordinary generated scene.

The shortcut fails concretely on canonical training pair 2 (zero-based pair index 1): two seeds share row 2 but an interior vertical 9 wall separates them. The no-wall shortcut paints nine cells that the authority leaves 0; its first mismatches are `(2,1)`, `(2,2)`, `(2,3)`, and `(2,4)` (zero-based coordinates). The same shortcut also disagrees with canonical pairs 3, 4, and the test pair. A curriculum made only from the current ordinary sampler therefore teaches intersection geometry but not the rule's line-of-sight blocker condition. I did not modify this audit target.

Evidence for the 85d01dd02c6d finding is retained in `checks/audit/85d01dd02c6d/input.json`, canonical Racket output `checks/audit/85d01dd02c6d/racket.json`, and `checks/audit/85d01dd02c6d/rival.json` (generator SHA-256 `70ed0afeeed58e4269be0ce7b3b07dda5f1107ab208dcdab7c12e8069b824a80`, rule hash `071ab7615984`). A fresh authority rerun is retained as `racket-final.json`; its `results` field is identical to `racket.json`.
